messages:
nina: FYI just got an escalation from AcmePayments (enterprise, Dedicated) — they see a p95 jump from ~180ms to ~650ms since last night. Sales flagged it as potentially customer-impacting. Can we triage and decide whether this becomes a product backlog priority?
carla: Thanks @nina. Can you paste the customer report and any repro steps? Do they have a pinned timeframe or be billed credits?
nina: Quote from account: 'sudden latency in transaction chat endpoint impacting user flows; started ~02:30 UTC; appears correlated with spike in qps to 4–5k/s.' They want ETA and mitigation. Account asks for temporary routing to Dedicated pool A if possible.
sam: Adding context from infra: we saw increased tail from a handful of Dedicated hosts in eu-west-1 starting 02:25 UTC. Kernel-level OOMs on one node, others had queueing. Logs show many small requests with 1–2 tokens causing overhead.
liam: Oncall checked node logs — one host hit high swap + long GC-like stalls in the runtime. Metric: host-42 cpu steal/softirq high. Not systemic across entire fleet but enough to push their p95 up.
carla: Product question: does customer want long-term SLA change or immediate mitigation? We should scope as two tracks: 1) immediate mitigation (workaround + incident fix) and 2) backlog item for platform hardening + routing policies.
nina: Customer asked for a short-term routing change and a longer-term assurance. Sales asks for a clear commitment window.
sam: For immediate: we can add a temporary routing rule to send routing keys for AcmePayments to their reserved DG pool with capacity buffer. That is operational, not product. But we should scope a product-facing feature: automatic per-customer overflow routing + throttling thresholds.
carla: I propose: create a product ticket for "per-tenant overflow routing + SLO protective throttle" and include acceptance criteria. If we can ship a minimal config UI + API for routing rules in 2 sprints, that covers customer ask. Short term: ops does manual routing change and alerting. Agree?
liam: Ops can do the manual routing now. I'll open the manual change with runbook and rollback and notify the customer. Also recommend we add an alert for queue depth per-dedicated-tenant.
alex: From runtime POV, we should also audit small-request overhead — we may be paying a lot of per-request fixed cost for these tiny tokens. We can add batching heuristics or prefix-KV caching for short calls; that is a separate eng project (size: small/medium).
carla: Let's capture scope and acceptance criteria for the product ticket. Suggested ACs: 1) UI+API to define per-tenant routing with priority and overflow target; 2) test plan + canary to validate failover without >=5% p95 regression for other tenants; 3) docs for runbook and SRE handoff. Thoughts?
sam: Add AC: expose metrics for routing decision (per-customer p95, qps, active hosts) and a guard to avoid routing loops.
liam: Add AC: automated alerting for per-tenant queue depth and host-level pressure with playbook link.
nina: Customer wants a firm ETA — can we promise "manual routing today, product feature in 4 weeks"? If we can scope an MVP in 4 weeks, sales will push that to the customer.
carla: I won't promise 4 weeks until we size properly. I can commit to "manual routing within 2h + product scoping doc by EOD". For timeline: estimate MVP in 3–6 sprints depending on engineering priority. We'll negotiate with sales.
sam: For prioritization, we need to know impact: how many customers would benefit and risk of recurring incidents. I can run a quick query to identify other tenants with similar qps patterns.
deploy-bot: deploy status: manual-routing-playbook v1 applied to AcmePayments - change window started by liam at 2026-03-21T03:10:05Z
liam: Manual routing applied. Early telemetry shows p95 dropping to ~220ms on their routed traffic. Monitoring for 30m.
carla: Great — I'll create the product ticket and include the ACs we discussed. Ticket will be shared in this thread and assigned to eng-platform for sizing. Nina, please update the customer with: manual mitigation applied, monitoring underway, scoping doc by EOD, and tentative roadmap window pending sizing.
nina: Sending update now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
carla: Action items: 1) carla: create product ticket + scoping doc by EOD; 2) sam + alex: quick telem query + runtime cost analysis; 3) liam: confirm monitoring stable and create alert rule; 4) nina: customer comms and expectation setting.
alex: I'll drop a short diagnostic snippet in the ticket showing per-request CPU cost and possible batchable paths.
sam: If the sizing looks small, let's try to prioritize for next milestone; otherwise we schedule it into the Q2 platform backlog.
liam: Monitoring looks stable at +10m, p95 ~230ms. I'll keep the manual routing in place until product feature exists or traffic normalizes.
carla: Thanks team. I'll post the ticket link here when ready and mark this thread as the intake record."
